statement: A rectangular field is bounded on one side by a wall. 100 m of fence is used for the other three sides. If the side parallel to the wall has length $x$ m, (i) show that the enclosed area is $A=\frac{x(100-x)}{2}$; (ii) find the value of $x$ that maximises $A$; (iii) find the maximum area.
solution: (i) If the side parallel to the wall is $x$, the two perpendicular sides are each $y=\frac{100-x}{2}$. Area $A=xy=\frac{x(100-x)}{2}$. (ii) $\frac{dA}{dx}=\frac{100-2x}{2}=50-x$, zero at $x=50$. Since $A$ is a downward parabola, this gives the maximum. (iii) Maximum area $=\frac{50\cdot 50}{2}=1250\ \text{m}^{2}$.
hints: Express the two equal sides in terms of x.
